text:
Owen Power is having the season Buffalo drafted him first overall to have. He has 18 points in 25 games, double last season's rate, and he's playing 25 minutes a night, up from about 21 and a half. He's also on the ice for 31% of the Sabres' power-play time, up from 12%, though he has yet to record a power-play point. That's the oddity in the line: the breakout has come almost entirely at even strength.

How much of it is real? Some of the point rate will cool; our talent range puts his true scoring closer to 1.2 points per 60 than the 1.72 he's posting. But the chances support him. The Sabres have scored 5.5 fewer goals than they deserve with him on the ice, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 96th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists last season. He sets teammates up.

One thing to watch: his minutes over the last ten games averaged 22.7, below his season mark. Whether that's game flow or a deliberate easing is worth following.
